correctness.rationale: Complete proof: (i) a group element fixes a realization point iff a nonempty orbit of arrow vertices spans a multipath face, by invariant positive barycentric support; (ii) rotations r^a have such an orbit iff gcd(n,a)>=2, since gcd=1 forces a full directed cycle and gcd>=2 supplies disjoint arrows kd->kd+1; (iii) all reflections fix a barycenter of the two disjoint mirrored arrows based on 1->2, verified separately for a=0 and a=1; (iv) Caputi–Collari–Smith Theorem 2.8 gives nu_n=floor((n-2)/2)-1>=1 for n>=6; (v) Armstrong 1965 theorem applies to connected simply connected finite simplicial realization and each finite subgroup, pi1=H/N_H. Every proper cyclic subgroup is generated by a fixed-point rotation; any subgroup with a reflection is generated by fixed-point elements. For full C_n the fixed-element exponents are exactly those sharing a nontrivial divisor with n: N=<r^p> if n=p^e and N=C_n if n has distinct prime factors. Abelianization gives integral H1. For prime p>=7 the C_p action is free. Connectivity gives H_b(X_p;Z)=0 for 1<=b<=nu_p=(p-5)/2. The integral Cartan–Leray spectral sequence collapses along the b=0 row in those degrees, yielding group homology of C_p, Z/p in odd degrees and 0 in even. Boundary cases n=6, p=7 checked; no finite experiment is used as infinite proof. Embedded verifier exhaustively tests fixed arrow-orbit membership and every dihedral subgroup for n=6..60 and independently computes quotient H1 over five fields for n=7, with exact chain condition.

originality.rationale: Primary arXiv:2601.05670v1 (2026-01-09) supplies original-complex connectivity and homology, not orbit-space fundamental groups or quotient torsion. The published 2026-10-11 note on dihedral rational homology (identifier 627013477864) explicitly treats reflection/rotation arrow orbits and rational characters, which are NOT claimed new here; it neither computes pi1 of orbit spaces nor any integral quotient H_j. Armstrong (1965) provides the general pi1 formula but not these stabilizer-generated subgroups, arithmetic prime-power transition, or complete subgroup classification; Cartan–Leray is used as a standard theorem but does not specify these prime-family torsion groups. Synthesis of these facts with a direct support-based proof, all-subgroup classification, and vanishing-line spectral sequence yields the new concrete object-specific theorem. Targeted actual searches found no previous equivalent classification. Residual risk: an unindexed equivalent or a general theorem specialized to these graph complexes could subsume the result, and the derivation uses classical general machinery.

value.rationale: The natural all-subgroup family of topological orbit spaces exhibits a sharp arithmetic transition: only full cyclic symmetry may retain π1, with order exactly the unique prime divisor if and only if n is a prime power, while every proper rotational quotient and every reflection-containing subgroup quotient is simply connected. For primes p, despite torsion-free high-connectivity of original complexes, the quotient has genuine integral Z/p torsion in every odd degree ≤(p−5)/2, furnishing arbitrarily many torsion dimensions. These integral fundamental-group and high-dimensional torsion invariants are invisible to previously known rational characters and individual Betti numbers. The exact all-parameter boundary provides a motivated structural classification, not a selected arbitrary finite sample or tiny numerical increment.
